question: Will João Campos win the Pernambuco Governor election?
rules:
The Pernambuco gubernatorial election is scheduled to take place in Brazil on October 4, 2026, with a runoff on October 25, 2026, if no candidate receives a majority of the valid votes in the first round.

This market will resolve according to the candidate who wins this election.

Temporary, interim, or placeholder governors appointed by any means before the specified election will not be considered.

If the result of this election isn't known by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Brazilian government, specifically the Superior Electoral Court (Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, TSE) (e.g., www.tse.jus.br/eleicoes/resultados-eleicoes).

evidence.excerpt: The Simplex/CBN stimulated first-round poll put Raquel Lyra at 45% and João Campos at 37.9%, with 11.1% unable or unwilling to answer and 4.6% choosing blank, null or none. In a two-candidate scenario, Lyra had 46.4% and Campos 39.9%. The survey interviewed 1,067 voters by telephone on September 16–20, 2026, with a three-percentage-point margin of error and 95% confidence, and was registered as PE-07901/2026.

João Campos's campaign was trying to secure a visit by President Lula to Pernambuco before the first round, but Lula had not confirmed it. Although Lula had declared support for Campos, the report described a non-aggression pact with Governor Raquel Lyra. Campos's allies regarded a presidential visit as decisive given his disadvantage in polling.

AtlasIntel measured Raquel Lyra at 48.7% and João Campos at 45.6% in the first round. Its runoff simulation put Lyra at 51.1% and Campos at 47.3%, described as a technical tie within the poll's two-percentage-point margin of error. The Bloomberg-commissioned survey recruited 1,793 voters digitally on September 11–16, with 95% confidence, and was registered as PE-02989/2026.

RealTime Big Data put João Campos at 44% and Raquel Lyra at 43% in the stimulated first round. Both candidates had 44% in the runoff simulation, with 6% choosing blank or null and 6% not knowing or not answering. The poll interviewed 1,600 people in Pernambuco on September 10–14, 2026, with a two-percentage-point margin of error and 95% confidence, under registration PE-07953/2026.

Datafolha put Raquel Lyra at 47% and João Campos at 42%, a technical tie within its three-percentage-point margin of error. Excluding blank, null and undecided responses, Lyra had 51% of valid votes and Campos 46%; a runoff simulation gave Lyra 51% and Campos 44%. The Folha/TV Globo survey interviewed 1,204 voters in 48 municipalities on September 8–10 and was registered under PE-04411/2026 and BR-05923/2026.

Quaest put Raquel Lyra at 43% and João Campos at 37%, compared with 44% and 36%, respectively, in its August 25 release. Undecided voters accounted for 12%, while blank, null and non-voting responses totaled 6%. The Globo-commissioned poll interviewed 1,302 Pernambuco voters on September 4–7, with a three-percentage-point margin of error and 95% confidence, and was registered as PE-00285/2026. Rejection was 40% for Campos and 34% for Lyra.

evidence.publisher: Tribunal Regional Eleitoral de Santa Catarina
evidence.excerpt: The 2026 general election was scheduled for October 4, including elections for governors. Any second round was scheduled for October 25. First-round free electoral advertising on radio and television was scheduled to begin August 28 and end October 1.

With all 3,409 polling sections totaled, João Campos of the PSB was reelected mayor of Recife in the first round of the 2024 municipal election. He received 725,721 votes, equivalent to 78.11% of valid votes.
